FLASHCARD SET · AGES 12–18 MONTHS

First Words: Food & Home Flashcards

Eleven cards for the Toddler 1 stage: the foods on the high-chair tray and the things in every room, named clearly so first words have somewhere to land.

These cards belong to Toddler 1 on the Kiddo School learning path.

Every card in the set.

Every card is right here on one page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Read every card right here.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Name it at the table

    Food cards work best at real meals. Apple card at breakfast, banana card at snack — the word arrives with the taste.

  2. 02

    The pause is the point

    Say the word, then wait three full seconds. First attempts sound like “ah!” and “mm!” — they count. Answer warmly.

  3. 03

    Two places per word

    Show the shoe card in the morning, then name real shoes at the door. Words repeated in two places stick twice as well.

  4. 04

    Let the toddler win

    Hand your toddler the card to hold, wave and crumple. A card that has been thoroughly loved is a card that has been learned.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST WORDS: FOOD & HOME · AGES 12–18 MONTHS

      Apple Flashcard for Toddlers

      A red apple, leading the food cards. By 12–18 months many toddlers have held, gummed and thrown an apple — the word has a lot of history to attach to.

      Teaching tips

      What this word card does

      Names the fruit your toddler already sees sliced, whole and thrown from the tray.

      Say it at the table

      Say apple at breakfast while the slices sit on the tray, once, clearly.

      What it builds

      Builds a first food vocabulary that grows straight off the highchair tray.

      Print it like this

      Print on cardstock; tray-side cards meet juice, so wipe-clean helps.

      Baby tip

      Answer every attempt warmly, from a full word to a hopeful babble.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the First Words for Toddlers 12–18 Months: Food & Home class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST WORDS: FOOD & HOME · AGES 12–18 MONTHS

      Banana Flashcard for Toddlers

      A yellow banana. Peelable, mashable and funny to say — banana often becomes a toddler favourite word purely on vibes.

      Teaching tips

      What this word card does

      Puts a funny-shaped favourite into word form, ready for snack time.

      Say it at the table

      Name the banana as it lands on the plate, then pause and wait.

      What it builds

      Strengthens repetition skills — funny words said often become firm favourites.

      Print it like this

      A sleeve of clear sticky plastic turns this one mash-proof.

      Baby tip

      Say it twice at most, then let the snack do the rest.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · FIRST WORDS: FOOD & HOME · AGES 12–18 MONTHS

      Orange Flashcard for Toddlers

      A bright orange. One word for the fruit and the colour — this card quietly teaches two ideas at once, the toddler way.

      Teaching tips

      What this word card does

      Carries a fruit and a shade inside the same single word.

      Say it at the table

      Say orange at the table, then again when the colour turns up on a toy.

      What it builds

      One word doing double duty, quietly teaching two ideas at once.

      Print it like this

      Bold and bright prints best — keep the fruit round and unmistakable.

      Baby tip

      One name for fruit and colour is fine — no explaining needed.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · FIRST WORDS: FOOD & HOME · AGES 12–18 MONTHS

      Milk cup Flashcard for Toddlers

      A cup of milk. For most toddlers this is the most meaningful object in the house — the card names the ritual.

      Teaching tips

      What this word card does

      Names the most wanted drink in the house, in the two words it gets called.

      Say it at the table

      Split the name at milk time — milk, small pause, cup — and pour.

      What it builds

      Introduces two-word names, the very first grammar your toddler will hear.

      Print it like this

      Cardstock again — this one earns its keep near the kitchen.

      Baby tip

      Keep it to the two words; longer sentences can wait months.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · FIRST WORDS: FOOD & HOME · AGES 12–18 MONTHS

      Bread Flashcard for Toddlers

      A loaf of bread. Soft, warm at the right moments and present at nearly every meal — bread is a comfort word.

      Teaching tips

      What this word card does

      Gives a soft, everyday food a name your toddler hears at most meals.

      Say it at the table

      Name the bread while the sandwich is made and your toddler watches.

      What it builds

      Grows kitchen vocabulary in the room where your toddler most wants to be.

      Print it like this

      Two copies work well — kitchen table plus the changing bag.

      Baby tip

      Meals are for eating first; a single naming per meal is plenty.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · FIRST WORDS: FOOD & HOME · AGES 12–18 MONTHS

      Egg Flashcard for Toddlers

      A simple egg. Small, oval and everywhere at breakfast — a tidy little word with a clear shape.

      Teaching tips

      What this word card does

      Cracks open a first word that shows up at the table every morning.

      Say it at the table

      Offer the word egg at breakfast, right as the real one appears.

      What it builds

      Sharpens shape noticing — one small oval, met fresh every morning.

      Print it like this

      Small is fine here; the egg reads clearly at any sensible size.

      Baby tip

      A cracked shell can startle; show it once slowly and carry on.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · FIRST WORDS: FOOD & HOME · AGES 12–18 MONTHS

      Cup Flashcard for Toddlers

      The family cup, back again. Your toddler has met this word in earlier sets — now it stands with the food words, where it lives every day.

      Teaching tips

      What this word card does

      Shows the object your toddler lifts with both hands at every drink.

      Say it at the table

      Hold the card near the highchair and say cup as the drink arrives.

      What it builds

      Strengthens recall — the picture names it before any voice needs to.

      Print it like this

      Laminate if spills are frequent — at this age, they will be.

      Baby tip

      Offer it calmly at each drink; no quizzing, no pressure to repeat.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · FIRST WORDS: FOOD & HOME · AGES 12–18 MONTHS

      Spoon Flashcard for Toddlers

      A trusty spoon. Another returning friend — spoon has been with your child since the first solids, and it is not going anywhere.

      Teaching tips

      What this word card does

      Names the tool that travels from tray to mouth so many times a day.

      Say it at the table

      Hand the spoon over with its name attached, calm and unhurried.

      What it builds

      Links naming to doing, since the spoon word arrives with a job.

      Print it like this

      Keep a copy in the kitchen drawer, next to the real thing.

      Baby tip

      Messy self-feeding is fine; the word and the meal both continue.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · FIRST WORDS: FOOD & HOME · AGES 12–18 MONTHS

      Shoe Flashcard for Toddlers

      A shoe, stepping over from the everyday set. Shoes mark transitions — outside, inside, off to the park — and toddlers feel those changes deeply.

      Teaching tips

      What this word card does

      Turns the twice-daily shoe routine into a word your toddler can own.

      Say it at the table

      Name each shoe at the door as it lands on its foot.

      What it builds

      Attaches words to daily transitions — shoes mean outside is coming.

      Print it like this

      Print at shoe-rack size and keep it by the front door.

      Baby tip

      Keep it cheerful at the door; the word survives a rushed morning.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · FIRST WORDS: FOOD & HOME · AGES 12–18 MONTHS

      Sock Flashcard for Toddlers

      A soft sock. Small, stretchy and often worn on hands as well as feet — sock is a word with texture in every sense.

      Teaching tips

      What this word card does

      Gives the littlest clothes item a name, right on the wiggly foot it covers.

      Say it at the table

      Slip the sock on with its name, then enjoy the kick that follows.

      What it builds

      Extends the clothes word family, one stretchy piece at a time.

      Print it like this

      Any paper will do, though thicker stock survives the laundry basket tour.

      Baby tip

      One naming per dressing is plenty — the wiggle does the rest.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · FIRST WORDS: FOOD & HOME · AGES 12–18 MONTHS

      Chair Flashcard for Toddlers

      A sturdy chair, closing the set. Your toddler’s throne at every meal — the biggest object in the set and a real milestone word: furniture!

      Teaching tips

      What this word card does

      Points at the seat where every meal happens — the set's biggest word yet.

      Say it at the table

      Try chair as the climbing word, said once at every mealtime settle.

      What it builds

      Completes a small world of names — food, clothes and one sturdy seat.

      Print it like this

      Full-page size suits this biggest card — it earns the wall space.

      Baby tip

      Whisper it at the climb-up moment, as they rise.

      Teach it, step by step
